tool_input.command:
git add internal/doctor/doctor.go internal/doctor/doctor_test.go && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(doctor): #5/#12 — dormant WARN restored for literal unmarked calls, Windows FAILs when no textual evidence exists

Leader ruling on PR #515's remaining findings:

#5: a dormant repo with a standalone, unmarked `ethos audit seal` call
— no BEGIN/END markers, so hasMarkerSection cannot see it — read a
plain PASS "not enabled here," collapsing gated-but-unenabled into
never-enabled. hasMarkerSection's OR looksLikeInvocation's now gates
the dormant WARN: both are pure lexical scans, no execution, staying
inside the dormant branch's documented "lexical is sufficient here"
rationale (P1/S2) and the kcbv stop-loss against lexical patches for
the execution-based path. This supersedes P5's pinned PASS for this
exact fixture; P5's underlying trade-off (don't execute hooks in
dormant repos) is untouched and still covers the narrower residual —
an eval-obscured or otherwise dynamically-assembled call, which no
lexical scan can see — pinned in a new test alongside the updated one.

#12: on Windows (the one platform this sandbox cannot execution-verify
at all), a hook with zero textual trace of the required call
downgraded all the way to an honest-sounding WARN, a real regression
from the pre-execution lexical check, which could at least catch that
case. The unsupported-platform branch now also runs
looksLikeInvocation: no textual evidence FAILs (this hook would not
pass even the old check); textual evidence present keeps the WARN,
since only execution can PROVE the call is live, not merely present.

Both regressions confirmed failing against pre-fix code (P5's fixture
returned PASS not WARN; the Windows no-evidence fixture returned WARN
not FAIL) before their fixes landed. Full TestCheckSealHook/
TestCheckTrailerHook suites green, race-tested.
EOF
)"
